sources.entry: SelfControl - macOS app to block your own access to distracting websites etc for a predetermined period of time. It can not be undone by the app or by a restart – you must wait for the timer to run out.

summary.one_liner: SelfControl is a free, open-source macOS app that blocks your own access to distracting websites and mail servers for a set period that cannot be ended early.
summary.what_it_does: Lets you set a block duration, add sites to a blocklist, and start the block with a "Start Block" button. Until the timer expires, the blocked sites stay inaccessible, even after a restart or deleting the application. The blocklist can include mail servers or anything else on the Internet, not just websites. The README describes it as available in 12 languages thanks to translators. Development builds are made from the source using CocoaPods and the selfcontrol.xcworkspace file.
use_cases: block distracting websites for a set time
focus and reduce procrastination on a Mac
commit to a timed internet-free work session
how_to_run: Clone the SelfControl repo from GitHub.
Make sure you have a recent version of Xcode and the Xcode command-line tools installed.
Install CocoaPods: sudo gem install cocoapods
Install the SelfControl dependencies using CocoaPods: pod install
Build and run (you may need to update/remove code signing settings to make it build properly)
stack: Objective-C/Swift (macOS app, inferred from Xcode build)
notable: Block cannot be undone by the app or by a restart; you must wait for the timer to run out
Blocks mail servers as well as websites and other Internet access
Free and open source under the GPL
Available in 12 languages through community translators
caveats: macOS only; development builds require a Mac running a modern macOS version
Users are directed to download the official release from the project website rather than building from source
Building requires code signing adjustments that may need manual changes
